_comment: English translation. Keys are the French texts shown by the app (interface + server data). To add a language, copy this file (e.g. es.json) and translate the values.

exact.pour lire la valeur mesurée, ou va voir: to read the measured value, or go see:
exact.Reconstitution 3D à partir de l'imagerie: 3D reconstruction from satellite imagery: this is NOT the satellite's camera
exact.Calcul des passages sur 3 jours…: Computing passes for the next 3 days…
exact.Aucun passage à plus de 10° d'élévation: No pass above 10° elevation in the next 3 days.
exact.Toujours en activité, pas de date de fin: Still active, no end date announced
exact.Aucune fiche publique détaillée pour cet: No detailed public file for this object (often the case for military or little-known commercial satellites).
exact.Émetteurs radio actifs (on peut les écou: Active radio transmitters (you can listen to them with an antenna and an SDR receiver):
exact.Caméra embarquée : images réelles du jou: Onboard camera: real images of the day
exact.Flux vidéo en direct de la chaîne YouTub: Live video stream from NASA's official YouTube channel. When the ISS is in Earth's shadow or loses signal, the screen may be black or show another broadcast.
exact.Mosaïque des images prises par l'instrum: Mosaic of the images taken by Terra's MODIS instrument on the chosen day, in natural colors (250 m resolution).
Mosaic of the images taken by Aqua's MODIS instrument on the chosen day, in natural colors (250 m resolution).
exact.Images de l'instrument VIIRS de Suomi NP: Images from Suomi NPP's VIIRS instrument on the chosen day (375 m resolution).
exact.Images de l'instrument VIIRS de NOAA-20: Images from NOAA-20's VIIRS instrument on the chosen day (375 m resolution).
exact.Images de l'instrument VIIRS de NOAA-21: Images from NOAA-21's VIIRS instrument on the chosen day (375 m resolution).
exact.Planètes : modèle VSOP87. Comètes et ast: Planets: VSOP87 model. Comets and asteroids: two-body Keplerian computation from JPL orbital elements.
exact.Prochain passage visible à l'œil nu: Next pass visible to the naked eye
exact.Pas de passage visible à l'œil nu dans l: No pass visible to the naked eye in the next 4 days (the ISS has to be sunlit while you are in the dark).
exact.Magnitude : plus le chiffre est petit, p: Magnitude: the smaller the number, the brighter the object (Venus ≈ −4, naked-eye limit ≈ +6). Uranus and Neptune need binoculars or a telescope.
exact.Calculés en direct, pas recopiés d'une l: Computed live, not copied from a list
exact.Jamais d'observation sans lunettes spéci: Never look without certified eclipse glasses (ISO 12312-2).
exact.ZHR : nombre de météores par heure dans: ZHR: meteors per hour under a perfect sky with the radiant at the zenith. In practice you see 2 to 3 times fewer. The Moon is the deciding factor.
exact.Astéroïdes qui frôlent la Terre (60 jour: Asteroids passing close to Earth (60 days)
exact.Source : NASA/JPL (CNEOS). 1 distance lu: Source: NASA/JPL (CNEOS). 1 lunar distance = 384,400 km. None of these objects threatens Earth.
exact.Uniquement de vraies images, avec leur d: Only real images, with the date they were taken
exact.Voir l'ISS sur le globe: See the ISS on the globe
exact.Les dernières photos prises par les astr: The latest photos taken by astronauts from the station, published by NASA.
exact.Flux en direct de la chaîne officielle d: Live stream from NASA's official channel. Black screen = the station is in Earth's shadow or has lost signal (it happens several times an hour).
exact.Le film est fabriqué uniquement avec les: The replay is made only from the astronauts' real photos: they often shoot bursts (one photo per second) while the station moves at 7.7 km/s. Played back to back, they show exactly what they saw, with the time and the location of every frame.
exact.Pour l'activer, il faut une clé gratuite: To enable it, you need a free key for NASA's photo database (
exact.avec pour objet « Photos Database API Ke: with the subject "Photos Database API Key Request", then put it in the variable
exact.Aucune séquence ce jour-là (les photos a: No sequence that day (photos are published a few days late).
exact.Le flux de l'agence est en retard ou en: The agency's feed is delayed or paused
exact.Galerie : la Lune et les planètes: Gallery: the Moon and the planets
exact.Chargement de la galerie (première fois: Loading the gallery (first time: analyzing images, about 30 s)…
exact.Vraie photo publiée par la NASA (pas de: Real photo published by NASA (no artist's view, map or simulation)
exact.La Lune ou une planète est le sujet nomm: The Moon or a planet is the subject named in the title
exact.Analyse de l'image : l'astre est seul, e: Image analysis: the body is alone, whole and sharp against the black background of space
exact.Des planètes en orbite autour d'autres é: Planets orbiting stars other than the Sun. The first one around a star like ours was found in 1995 (51 Pegasi b).
exact.Source : NASA Exoplanet Archive. al = an: Source: NASA Exoplanet Archive. ly = light-years.
exact.La géolocalisation n'est pas disponible: Geolocation is not available on this device.
exact.Station spatiale internationale (États-U: International Space Station (USA, Russia, Europe, Japan, Canada), continuously crewed since November 2000.
exact.Laboratoire en microgravité : biologie,: Microgravity laboratory: biology, medicine, fluid physics, materials, Earth observation. French astronauts Thomas Pesquet (2016-2017 and 2021) and Sophie Adenot (2026) have lived aboard.
exact.Fin de vie prévue vers 2030 : elle sera: End of life planned around 2030: it will be deorbited over the Pacific by a SpaceX tug.
exact.Internet haut débit par satellite (Space: High-speed satellite internet (SpaceX). Thousands of satellites in low orbit form a global mesh, linked to each other by lasers.
exact.Ne récolte pas de données scientifiques: Collects no scientific data: it relays internet traffic between ground antennas.
exact.Durée de vie d'environ 5 ans, puis désor: Lifetime of about 5 years, then deliberate deorbit: it burns up in the atmosphere.
exact.Internet par satellite (Eutelsat OneWeb): Satellite internet (Eutelsat OneWeb), orbit at ~1,200 km, mostly for businesses, planes and ships.
exact.Constellation Internet d'Amazon (projet: Amazon's internet constellation (Project Kuiper), a Starlink competitor.
exact.Téléphonie et messagerie satellite parto: Satellite phone and messaging anywhere on Earth, poles included (66 satellites).
exact.Communications ; porte aussi des récepte: Communications; also carries ADS-B receivers that track planes over the oceans.
exact.Téléphonie satellite et balises de détre: Satellite phone and distress beacons (iPhone emergency SOS via satellite).
exact.Messagerie pour objets connectés (suivi: Messaging for connected devices (tracking containers, ships, machinery).
exact.Messages courts et signaux AIS des navir: Short messages and AIS signals from ships.
exact.Système GPS américain : 31 satellites à: The American GPS system: 31 satellites at 20,200 km that give the position of any receiver on Earth.
exact.Émet en continu l'heure exacte de ses ho: Continuously broadcasts the exact time of its atomic clocks; the receiver computes its position by comparing the travel times of 4 or more signals.
exact.Signaux horaires d'horloges atomiques po: Atomic clock time signals used to compute positions.
exact.Galileo, le GPS européen, plus précis qu: Galileo, Europe's GPS, more precise than the American GPS (meter-level for the public).
exact.Signaux de navigation d'horloges atomiqu: Navigation signals from atomic clocks; also relays distress beacons (SAR service).
exact.Satellite russe de la série Cosmos (navi: Russian satellite of the Cosmos series (GLONASS navigation, military or scientific depending on the number).
exact.BeiDou, le système de navigation chinois: BeiDou, the Chinese navigation system (45+ satellites).
exact.Copernicus (UE/ESA) : radar qui photogra: Copernicus (EU/ESA): a radar that images the Earth day and night, through clouds.
exact.Images radar : glissements de terrain, i: Radar images: landslides, floods, sea ice, ground deformation after earthquakes.
exact.Copernicus (UE/ESA) : imagerie optique h: Copernicus (EU/ESA): high-resolution optical imagery of land.
exact.Images en 13 bandes de couleur (dont l'i: Images in 13 color bands (including infrared): crops, forests, fires, urban growth.
exact.Température et couleur des océans, haute: Ocean temperature and color, sea level, wildfires.
exact.Copernicus (UE/ESA) : qualité de l'air e: Copernicus (EU/ESA): air quality and atmospheric composition.
exact.Instrument TROPOMI : mesure chaque jour: TROPOMI instrument: measures nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), ozone (O₃), methane (CH₄), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO₂) and aerosols every day, by analyzing sunlight reflected by the Earth (absorption spectroscopy).
exact.Copernicus : mesure du niveau des océans: Copernicus: measures sea level to the centimeter.
exact.Satellites météo américains (NOAA) en or: American weather satellites (NOAA) in polar orbit.
exact.Images des nuages, températures et humid: Cloud images, atmospheric temperature and humidity for weather forecasts.
exact.Satellites météo européens (EUMETSAT) en: European weather satellites (EUMETSAT) in polar orbit.
exact.Profils de température et d'humidité, ve: Temperature and humidity profiles, ocean surface winds, ozone.
exact.Satellites météo européens géostationnai: European geostationary weather satellites, fixed above Africa and Europe.
exact.Une image complète du disque terrestre t: A full image of the Earth's disk every 10 to 15 minutes (the pictures you see in TV weather forecasts).
exact.Images des nuages en continu, éclairs, é: Continuous cloud images, lightning, solar flares.
exact.Programme américain d'observation des te: American land-observation program since 1972: the longest record of images of the Earth.
exact.Images multispectrales : évolution des f: Multispectral images: how forests, cities and glaciers have changed over 50 years.
exact.Nanosatellites Planet (format CubeSat) q: Planet nanosatellites (CubeSats) that photograph the whole Earth every day.
Images and videos at ~50 cm resolution.
exact.Module central de la station spatiale ch: Core module of China's Tiangong space station.
exact.Expériences scientifiques en microgravit: Scientific experiments in microgravity; crewed by 3 taikonauts.
exact.Images et spectres dans le visible, l'ul: Images and spectra in visible, ultraviolet and near-infrared light: the age of the Universe, accelerating expansion, exoplanet atmospheres.
exact.Débris spatial : morceau d'un satellite: Space debris: a piece of a satellite or rocket with no function at all.
exact.Rien. C'est un danger pour les satellite: Nothing. It's a danger to active satellites: at 7-8 km/s, even a fragment a few centimeters wide can destroy a satellite.
exact.Étage de fusée resté en orbite après avo: Rocket stage left in orbit after releasing its satellite.
exact.Rien. Il finira par retomber et brûler d: Nothing. It will eventually fall back and burn up in the atmosphere, sooner or later depending on its altitude.
exact.Zone de lancement en mer de Jeju (Corée: Jeju Island sea launch area (South Korea)
exact.La plus célèbre des comètes. Revient tou: The most famous comet. Returns every ~76 years, next in 2061. Its dust creates the Orionids and the Eta Aquariids.
exact.La comète à la période la plus courte co: The comet with the shortest known period (3.3 years). Parent of the Taurids.
exact.« La comète du diable », visible à l'œil: The "devil comet", visible to the naked eye in spring 2024.
exact.Comète mère des Draconides, survolée par: Parent comet of the Draconids, flown by the ICE probe in 1985.
exact.Comète mère des Léonides, responsable de: Parent comet of the Leonids, behind the meteor storms of 1833, 1966 and 2001.
exact.Visitée par la sonde Rosetta (ESA). Le r: Visited by the Rosetta probe (ESA). The Philae lander touched down on it in 2014: a first.
exact.Comète mère des Perséides. Noyau de 26 k: Parent comet of the Perseids. A 26 km nucleus, one of the largest objects that regularly crosses Earth's orbit.
exact.Hale-Bopp, visible à l'œil nu pendant 18: Hale-Bopp, visible to the naked eye for 18 months in 1996-1997. Won't be back for ~2,400 years.
NEOWISE, the great comet of summer 2020.
exact.ʻOumuamua (2017) : premier objet venu d': ʻOumuamua (2017): the first object from another star system ever detected.
exact.Borisov (2019) : première comète interst: Borisov (2019): the first confirmed interstellar comet.
exact.3I/ATLAS (2025) : troisième visiteur int: 3I/ATLAS (2025): the third interstellar visitor, discovered on July 1, 2025.
exact.Cérès, planète naine et plus gros objet: Ceres, a dwarf planet and the largest object in the asteroid belt. Explored by the Dawn probe.
exact.Vesta, le deuxième plus gros astéroïde,: Vesta, the second-largest asteroid, also visited by Dawn.
exact.Apophis : passera à ~32 000 km de la Ter: Apophis: will pass ~32,000 km from Earth on April 13, 2029, below the orbit of geostationary satellites. No risk of impact.
exact.Bennu : échantillon ramené sur Terre par: Bennu: a sample was brought back to Earth by the OSIRIS-REx probe in 2023.
exact.Ryugu : échantillon ramené par la sonde: Ryugu: a sample was brought back by the Japanese Hayabusa2 probe in 2020.
exact.Didymos : sa lune Dimorphos a été percut: Didymos: its moon Dimorphos was hit by the DART probe in 2022, the first planetary defense test.
exact.Phaéton : un astéroïde qui produit une p: Phaethon: an asteroid that produces a meteor shower, the Geminids.
exact.2003 EH1 : probable comète éteinte, mère: 2003 EH1: probably an extinct comet, parent of the Quadrantids.
exact.Orbite géostationnaire, 35 786 km, au-de: Geostationary orbit, 35,786 km, above the Atlantic
Geostationary orbit, 35,786 km, above the Pacific
exact.Imageur ABI en couleurs naturelles (GeoC: ABI imager in natural colors (GeoColor). One image every 10 minutes: you can watch hurricanes form.
exact.Même imageur que GOES-19, côté Pacifique: Same imager as GOES-19, on the Pacific side: western Americas, Hawaii, New Zealand.
exact.DSCOVR / EPIC : la Terre vue de 1,5 mill: DSCOVR / EPIC: the Earth seen from 1.5 million km
exact.Point de Lagrange L1, entre la Terre et: Lagrange point L1, between the Earth and the Sun
exact.La caméra EPIC voit en permanence la fac: The EPIC camera always sees the sunlit side of the Earth. A few times a year, the Moon passes in front.
exact.Orbite géosynchrone inclinée, sonde Sola: Inclined geosynchronous orbit, Solar Dynamics Observatory probe
exact.Ultraviolet extrême : on voit le plasma: Extreme ultraviolet: you can see 600,000 °C plasma following magnetic field loops.
exact.Couche à environ 50 000 °C : protubéranc: A layer at about 50,000 °C: prominences and filaments on the Sun's edge.
exact.Lumière visible : le Soleil tel qu'on le: Visible light: the Sun as you'd see it through a filter, with its dark spots.
exact.SOHO / LASCO C2 : la couronne proche: SOHO / LASCO C2: the inner corona
exact.Coronographe : un disque cache le Soleil: Coronagraph: a disk blocks the Sun to reveal its corona and coronal mass ejections.
exact.SOHO / LASCO C3 : le champ large: SOHO / LASCO C3: the wide field
exact.Champ de 30 diamètres solaires : on y vo: A field 30 solar diameters wide: you can see stars, planets close to the Sun and "sungrazing" comets.
exact.Flux vidéo en direct de la chaîne YouTub: Live video from NASA's official YouTube channel (black when the station is in Earth's shadow).
exact.Gaz brun-rouge émis surtout par les mote: A reddish-brown gas mostly emitted by engines, power plants and industry. It only lasts a few hours, so you can almost directly see cities, highways and ports.
Irritates the lungs and worsens asthma. It also helps form ground-level ozone.
exact.Craché par les volcans, les centrales à: Spewed by volcanoes, coal power plants and smelters. Volcanic plumes are spectacular: they can be seen over thousands of kilometers.
exact.Irritant respiratoire, et il retombe en: A respiratory irritant, and it falls back as acid rain.
exact.Produit par toutes les combustions incom: Produced by any incomplete combustion, especially forest and savanna fires. Measured around 5,500 m altitude, where winds carry it from one continent to another.
exact.Toxique à forte dose. Ici c'est surtout: Toxic at high doses. Here it mostly tracks large wildfires.
exact.Deuxième gaz à effet de serre après le C: The second greenhouse gas after CO₂: livestock, rice paddies, wetlands, gas and oil leaks. Over 20 years it warms about 80 times more than CO₂.
exact.Pas toxique à ces niveaux, mais c'est un: Not toxic at these levels, but a powerful greenhouse gas.
exact.L'épaisseur optique des aérosols : à que: Aerosol optical depth: how much particles (smoke, desert dust, pollution, sea salt) block light. 0.1 = very clean sky, above 1 = opaque sky.
exact.Les particules fines pénètrent profondém: Fine particles get deep into the lungs and the bloodstream.
exact.La quantité totale d'ozone au-dessus de: The total amount of ozone above us, mostly in the stratosphere, where it shields us from UV. Below 220 Dobson units, we speak of an ozone hole (over Antarctica in the southern spring).
exact.Moins d'ozone en altitude = plus d'UV au: Less ozone up high = more UV on the ground (sunburns, skin cancers).
exact.Pas de mesure ici ce jour-là (nuages, nu: No measurement here that day (clouds, night, or a gap between two satellite passes).
exact.Aucune mesure dans un rayon de ~15 km su: No measurement within ~15 km over the last 7 days (persistent clouds, polar night or no coverage).
No usable data at this location.
exact.Clique sur un lancement pour son dossier: Click a launch for its full file: where it lifts off from, when, where it goes, who runs it, the crew, the rocket, the weather and the sources.
exact.Sources : The Space Devs (Launch Library: Sources: The Space Devs (Launch Library 2), Open-Meteo, CelesTrak, J. McDowell's GCAT catalog.
exact.Délai depuis le tir précédent ici: Time since the previous launch here
exact.Voir le pas de tir sur le globe: See the pad on the globe
No public log for this launch.
exact.Repères indicatifs (chaque lanceur a ses: Indicative thresholds (each launcher has its own rules). Source: Open-Meteo.
exact.Recherche des objets mis en orbite…: Looking for the objects placed in orbit…
exact.Cet objet n'est pas (ou plus) dans le ca: This object is not (or no longer) in the tracked catalog: it may have re-entered or be too recent.
exact.Prévision disponible seulement dans les: Forecast only available within 15 days of liftoff.
exact.Pas encore de désignation internationale: No international designation yet (it's assigned after launch).
exact.Entre 200 et 2 000 km d'altitude, un tou: Between 200 and 2,000 km altitude, one orbit takes about 90 minutes. Home of the ISS, Starlink and most Earth-observation satellites.
exact.Orbite polaire vers 500-800 km, calée su: A polar orbit around 500-800 km, locked to the Sun: the satellite passes over each place at the same solar time every day. Perfect for comparing images day after day.
exact.Passe au-dessus des deux pôles : avec la: Passes over both poles: as the Earth turns underneath, the satellite ends up flying over the whole planet.
exact.Orbite très allongée (200 km au plus bas: A very stretched orbit (200 km at its lowest, 36,000 km at its highest). The satellite then uses its own engine to reach geostationary orbit.
exact.À 35 786 km au-dessus de l'équateur, le: 35,786 km above the equator, the satellite turns at the same speed as the Earth: it looks motionless in the sky. Telecoms and weather.
exact.Entre 2 000 et 35 000 km. C'est l'orbite: Between 2,000 and 35,000 km. The orbit of navigation systems: GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, BeiDou.
exact.Orbite très allongée qui permet de reste: A very stretched orbit that lets a satellite linger over one region (e.g. the Molniya orbit for Russia).
exact.Injection translunaire : la fusée quitte: Trans-lunar injection: the rocket leaves Earth orbit to reach the Moon, about 384,000 km away.
Placed in orbit around the Moon.
exact.Trajectoire interplanétaire vers Mars :: An interplanetary trajectory to Mars: 6 to 9 months of travel. Only possible every 26 months, when Earth and Mars line up.
exact.Trajectoire héliocentrique : la sonde qu: A heliocentric trajectory: the probe escapes Earth's gravity to orbit the Sun.
exact.La fusée monte dans l'espace puis retomb: The rocket goes up to space then falls back without circling the Earth.
exact.À 1,5 million de km vers le Soleil, un p: 1.5 million km toward the Sun, a balance point where a probe can stay between the Earth and the Sun.
exact.À 1,5 million de km à l'opposé du Soleil: 1.5 million km away from the Sun, where the James Webb telescope sits.
exact.L'heure de décollage est confirmée par d: Current T-0 confirmed by official or reliable sources.
exact.Une date est annoncée, mais pas encore c: A date has been announced but not yet officially confirmed.
exact.La date reste incertaine : elle peut enc: The date is still uncertain and may change a lot.
exact.La charge utile a été placée sur l'orbit: The payload was placed in the planned orbit.
exact.Le lancement n'a pas atteint son objecti: The launch did not reach its goal.
exact.La charge utile a été placée sur une orb: The payload was placed in a different orbit than planned.
The rocket is flying right now.
